description: The untrusted page webviews of Browser > Webview (labels `browser-page-*`, children of the `browser-host` window). A DENY capability, and that word is the whole story. The brief asked for the mirror of athena-portable's `capabilities/page.json` -- one grant, `allow-browser-page-reply`, and nothing else -- and that file cannot be written here: an app command's `allow-*` permission is generated only by `tauri_build::Attributes::app_manifest`, which `src-tauri/build.rs` does not use, and `cargo check` refuses the capability with `Permission allow-browser-page-reply not found` (measured 2026-09-15). Turning the app manifest on would ACL-gate all 1,656 commands app-wide, which is not WP2's decision. What stands in its place costs nothing and is stronger than it sounds: Tauri ACL-checks EVERY invoke from a remote origin whether or not an app manifest exists (tauri-2.11.2/src/webview/mod.rs:1822), so a page webview already reaches no app command at all, and `capabilities/default.json` is scoped to the `main` window, which these webviews are not in. This file is the belt to that brace -- an explicit deny of the core surfaces that would matter the day somebody widens `default.json` to `windows: ["*"]`, which is exactly the change that would otherwise hand the command surface to whatever site the operator last opened. The consequence to decide above this package: `browser_page_reply` is refused by the same rule, so the page -> shell direction of the relay is inert until an app manifest or an in-tree plugin gives it a permission to be granted. See docs/architecture/browser-control.md section 2a.
